question: Which welding process is most suitable for joining titanium alloys in aerospace applications due to its ability to provide an inert atmosphere and prevent oxidation?
options: Shielded Metal Arc Welding (SMAW)
Gas Tungsten Arc Welding (GTAW)
Flux-Cored Arc Welding (FCAW)
Submerged Arc Welding (SAW)

question: When performing a tensile test on a welded joint, the specimen fractures in the base metal rather than the weld zone. What does this indicate?
options: The weld metal has lower tensile strength than the base metal
The weld joint efficiency is less than 100%
The weld metal has equal or greater tensile strength than the base metal
The heat-affected zone is over-hardened

question: In accordance with AWS D1.1 Structural Welding Code, what is the minimum preheat temperature required for welding A514 steel with a thickness greater than 2.5 inches?
Which type of weld discontinuity is characterized by a groove melted into the base metal adjacent to the weld toe and left unfilled by weld metal?
options: Porosity
Undercut
Overlap
Incomplete fusion

question: A fabricator is producing a pressure vessel that requires post-weld heat treatment (PWHT). What is the primary purpose of PWHT in this application?
options: To increase the hardness of the weld zone
To improve the aesthetic appearance of the weld bead
To relieve residual stresses and restore toughness in the heat-affected zone
To eliminate all porosity within the weld metal

question: When calculating the throat dimension of a fillet weld with equal legs of 12mm, what is the theoretical throat size?
In plasma arc welding (PAW), what distinguishes the transferred arc mode from the non-transferred arc mode?
options: In transferred arc mode, the arc is established between the electrode and the nozzle only
In transferred arc mode, the arc is established between the electrode and the workpiece, making the workpiece part of the electrical circuit
In non-transferred arc mode, the workpiece is the positive terminal of the circuit
In transferred arc mode, higher gas flow rates are used exclusively for cutting

question: Which destructive test method is specifically used to evaluate the ductility and soundness of a weld by bending the specimen over a specified radius to detect surface cracks?
options: Charpy impact test
Nick-break test
Guided bend test
Macro-etch test

question: In GMAW, what welding parameter change will most directly result in a transition from globular transfer to spray transfer mode when using a CO2/Argon shielding gas mixture?
options: Decreasing wire feed speed below the transition current
Increasing voltage and current above the critical transition threshold
Reducing the argon content in the shielding gas mixture below 75%
Decreasing the contact tip to work distance significantly

question: A weld symbol on an engineering drawing shows a fillet weld with the weld-all-around symbol and a tail with the notation 'BSISI.' What does the weld-all-around circle on the reference line indicate?
options: The weld is to be performed in the field rather than the shop
The weld is to be applied continuously around the entire joint perimeter
The weld requires a backing bar on all sides
The weld must be inspected using radiographic testing on all sides

question: Which nondestructive testing (NDT) method is most effective for detecting subsurface planar discontinuities such as lack of fusion and cracks oriented parallel to the surface in thick-section welds?
options: Liquid penetrant testing (PT)
Magnetic particle testing (MT)
Ultrasonic testing (UT)
Visual inspection (VT)

question: When developing a Welding Procedure Specification (WPS) under ASME Section IX, which variable, if changed beyond the specified range, requires requalification of the procedure?
options: A supplementary essential variable when impact testing is required
A non-essential variable within the allowable range
A change in the weld position that is already qualified
A minor revision to the preheat temperature within the qualified range

question: In electroslag welding (ESW), what is the primary heat source that melts the base metal and filler wire?
options: An electric arc maintained between the electrode and the base metal
Resistance heating generated by the passage of current through the molten slag pool
An oxy-fuel flame directed into the joint
Induction heating coils surrounding the weld joint

question: A welder is fabricating a structural component using SAW and notices excessive convexity of the weld bead. Which combination of parameter adjustments would most effectively reduce bead convexity?
options: Increase travel speed and decrease wire feed speed
Increase voltage and decrease travel speed
Decrease voltage and increase current
Increase wire diameter and flux depth only

question: When performing radiographic testing (RT) on a circumferential weld of a pipe, what is the purpose of placing Image Quality Indicators (IQIs) on the source side of the weld?
options: To measure the actual thickness of the weld reinforcement
To verify the geometric unsharpness meets the required standard
To demonstrate that the radiographic technique has sufficient sensitivity to detect the minimum required discontinuity size
To identify the location of the weld centerline on the film
